uslaw-usc-t2-s288l:
Section 288l of Title 2 of the United States Code sets procedural rules for Senate legal counsel in court. Title 2 covers Congress, and this section sits in the chapter on the Office of Senate Legal Counsel. The hosted text is the version current in twenty twenty six. It governs how counsel may join a pending case.

Permission to intervene as a party, or to appear as a friend of the court, is a matter of right under a linked section. A court may deny it only on an express finding of set grounds. Those grounds are that the step is untimely and would greatly delay the pending action, or a like harm. Senate counsel thus has a strong statutory door into relevant cases.
